page: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system provides 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 7,600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all placing in the top 10% tier. The processor's advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), enables top-tier performance in extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read-only operations and uncached large-block read-only operations reaching the top 10% tier. Single-core performance is moderately lower, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier, indicating a tradeoff where the instance's strength lies heavily in parallelized multi-threaded execution rather than single-threaded speed.

The c8id.32xlarge demonstrates high resource density for compute-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. Its top-tier performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput makes it highly suitable for high-throughput databases and web serving. The inclusion of 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides high-speed local data access without the latency of network-attached storage, enhancing cost efficiency for data-intensive operations. Additionally, the instance performs exceptionally well in large-scale software compilation, ray tracing, and LLM inference prompt processing, making it a strong fit for parallel build systems, rendering, and CPU-based machine learning workloads.
